When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and a element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with paddings/margins between sections.

Try to do a lot of this planning and iteration in your thinking, and only show ideas to the user when you have higher confidence it'll delight them.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let the signature element be the one memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Not taking a risk can be a risk itself! Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots if your environment supports it – a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creators have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand, and therefore easier to use. They are design material, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality to copy that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's side of the screen. Name things by what people control and recognize, never by how the system is built. A person manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A control should say exactly what happens when it's used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the register conversational and tuned: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each element do exactly one job. A label labels, an example demonstrates, and nothing quietly does double duty.

At judging a judge picks an `account_id` and a twist card, and the engine runs live in about five minutes: 1. **Know the customer.** Any account shows typical income I, fixed costs F, spending S, savings buffer B, household bills H, loan payment P, gap, and months of runway, all from the precomputed profile artifact. 2. **Take a shock.** A shock (job loss with EI at 55 percent, bills up 15 percent, a one-off repair, or a mix) changes income or spending and the runway recomputes with the judge's branch rules. 3. **Make a plan.** A goal plan (emergency fund) and a backup plan (if the shock lands) built from the same numbers. The one-minute pitch opens with the Storm Atlas: the runway distribution across all 4,500 accounts, then one click drills into any account for the live twist. Every number a judge sees traces back to source rows through provenance checksums. The orbit game and the findings-first report framing are dropped as surfaces; their machinery may be reused internally. ## Hard constraints - **Judge definitions are the contract.** I, F, S, B, H, P and the runway come from docs/tangerine-challenge.md. Any deviation must be deliberate, documented in docs/decisions.md, and explainable to a judge. - **Integer cents end to end.** Dollars convert with `np.rint(dollars * 100)` once at load; every metric, mean, median and runway division afterwards is integer arithmetic with ROUND_HALF_UP (ties away from zero). No float may decide a branch. - **Deterministic offline artifact.** profiles.json carries no timestamps, no randomness, and no floats; two consecutive builds are byte identical. All data is bundled for an offline booth. - **Checksummed sources fail loud.** The three canonical CSVs are verified against data/tangerine/SHA256SUMS before any row is read. - **Any account must work.** All 4500 accounts, including the five edge flags (pensioner, thin history, zero income, defaulted loan, negative buffer), must render without a special case. - **One weather vocabulary.** src/lib/verdict.ts owns the five bands (critical, storm warning, watch, fair skies, clear) over integer deci months (10, 30, 60, 120). The deprecated seven-state ladder (weatherState.ts) was deleted in E5; no surface may reintroduce it. - **Honest sentences.** A sentence can never claim a twist the numbers did not run; scenario wording derives from the same Twist object the math ran (stormAtlas.shockedAtlasScenario). - **Content convention:** no em dashes, en dashes, minus signs, double hyphens, or spaced hyphens in shipped strings. verify.py scans the artifact and dashScan.test.ts scans the site strings. - **Static hosting only.** GitHub Pages, no server, no runtime network calls beyond bundled assets. ## Stack - Python 3.14 + uv + pandas + numpy for the offline engine pipeline; pytest for tests. Modules are header-style, snake_case, type hinted. - React 19, Vite 6, TypeScript 5.7 strict, Tailwind 3.4, Zustand 5, Vitest for the site. - three 0.170 + @react-three/fiber is legacy from the dropped game layer; not part of the engine surface. - GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions, base path aware. ## Phases E1 to E7 - **E1 profile precompute (COMPLETE).** scripts/engine writes public/data/engine/profiles.json (meta plus one profile per account). - **E2 console base (COMPLETE).** Account lookup, baseline card, shock presets plus sliders, verdict, plan text. - **E3 weather viz (COMPLETE).** Forecast strip, storm front, landfall pin, verdict bands, EI-cliff overlay. - **E4 plan engine (IN FLIGHT).** Goal math plus backup levers with +N months effects; golden_plans.json cross-language drift guard. - **E5 Storm Atlas (IN FLIGHT).** Population headline plus strip-plot drill-down, bank-wide scenario mode. - **E6 judge mode.** Keyboard shortcuts, edge-account guards, rehearsal, and paper fallback. - **E7 Solana A+ touch.** Gated memo package plus honest receipt badge in the verdict card. ## Data layer ``` data/tangerine/*.csv (checksums in SHA256SUMS) -> scripts/engine/load.py (verify, integer cent parse, grouping) -> scripts/engine/metrics.py (pure I, F, S, B, H, gap, flags) -> scripts/engine/shocks.py (pure runway function) -> scripts/engine/build.py (meta + profiles, deterministic) -> public/data/engine/profiles.json -> scripts/engine/verify.py (naive csv recompute, drift diff, SHA256) ``` - Sources: monthly_summary.csv (185,326 rows), loans.csv (682), accounts.csv (4,500), over 2020-01 to 2025-12. - The artifact: about 4.7 MB compact JSON, 4500 profiles, meta block with sources, definitions, checksum recipe, and edge flag counts. - Provenance: each profile carries a check_sum over `account_id:month` rows and `money_in` cents, recipe in pipeline_lib.checksum and mirrored by src/data/checksum.ts. ## Verification - `uv run python -m scripts.engine.build` and `uv run python -m scripts.engine.verify` (independent naive recompute, dash scan, SHA256, exit non zero on drift). - `uv run pytest -q`: golden fixtures pinned to both metrics.pipeline and the shipped artifact; determinism; check_sum recomputation. - `npx vitest run`: shock math pinned to golden_fixtures.json and golden_plans.json (TS and Python twins), 4500-profile cross checks, atlas conservation tests (every account exactly once, bins sum to 4500), deterministic plot jitter, headline honesty cases, dash scan. ## Frontend layering 1. **Data (src/data):** typed loaders with schema validation, checksum mirror, resolveRows. No math, no React. 2. **Core (src/lib):** pure functions only. Shock math (shocks.ts), plan math (planMath.ts), forecast (forecast.ts), verdict bands (verdict.ts), atlas counting/headline (stormAtlas.ts) and plot prep (atlasPlot.ts) live here; integer cents, never React. 3. **Views (src/components):** console (console/), weather (weather/), Storm Atlas (atlas/). Views render finished numbers; inline money math in a component is a review failure. 4. **Render:** presentation only, swappable without touching layers 1 to 3. Load once, memoize: profiles.json is fetched a single time and parsed once per session. App mounts the Atlas section above the console (id="atlas", id="console"); dot clicks route through the existing consoleStore.selectAccount, so E5 requires no store change and E6 key listeners remain the only store-adjacent E6 surface. ## Storm Atlas (E5 design, in flight) - The pitch opens with the population finding: the headline sentence quotes the share of accounts under 3.0 months of runway (critical + storm warning) at baseline, or under the live twist with a label derived from the same Twist the math ran; a comparison subline keeps the baseline number visible when a twist is live. - Five verdict-band cells show counts and whole percents; the strip plot renders every account as one dot on a six-segment axis aligned to the band edges (0-1, 1-3, 3-6, 6-12, 12-120 months, and a labeled 120+ overflow segment for the 1200 deci cap). Dot jitter is deterministic (FNV-1a over account_id). - Scenario mode runs applyTwist over all 4,500 accounts in one useMemo (about 2 to 5 ms), so the atlas re-colors live under a bank-wide shock: "if everyone gets this twist, N accounts hit critical". - Drill-down: a dot click selects that account in the console and scrolls to it; the strip is pointer-first and the console lookup is the capability-equal keyboard path. ## Performance budget - Artifact: profiles.json under 5 MB, single request, parse once; id index search under 10 ms. - Shock recalculation: integer arithmetic, under 1 ms per interaction for one account; the atlas population pass is about 2 to 5 ms per twist change inside one useMemo. - Everything bundled for offline booths; network allowed as a bonus, never a dependency. ## Gemini shock input (gated add-on, post E2) A typed-shock path where a judge's sentence maps to the shared ShockSpec (incomeFactor, billsPct, oneOffMonths, display-only duration) feeding the same Twist consumer as the presets. shockParse.ts owns the parse boundary; pendingShock never writes twist; confirmTypedShock is the single gate into state. Plain fetch to the generativelanguage.googleapis.com generateContent endpoint (no SDK, CORS), model gemini-3.5-flash-lite or 3.6-flash with thinkingLevel minimal and store false, strict JSON responseSchema. Key in import.meta.env.VITE_GEMINI_KEY, inlined, never printed. Hard 3 second AbortSignal.timeout, automatic fallback to preset cards on any failure, mode badge always shows the origin of the applied shock. Prompt payload: sentence, account_id, six baseline metrics (approved Nov 07 2026). Booth abort condition and full field ranges: see the E2-era architecture snapshot in git history and docs/decisions.md. ``` ## Ready-to-land: `docs/decisions.md` entry (append to end) ```markdown ## Nov 07 2026, Phase E5: Atlas fold onto verdict bands and the banded strip plot **Context**: the atlas scaffold counted the deprecated seven-state ladder (weatherState.ts, quarantined since E3) and had no strip-plot data, while the pitch must open with the runway distribution across all 4,500 accounts and drill into one account for the live twist. **Decision**: delete weatherState.ts and its tests outright (verdict.ts already owns labels, glyphs and thresholds; a wrapper would only re-serve them and keep dead state names alive). Reband stormAtlas.ts onto the five verdict bands; the default headline quotes under 3.0 months of runway (critical plus storm warning), and scenario wording derives from the same Twist object applyTwist runs via shockedAtlasScenario, so a sentence can never claim a twist the numbers did not run. New pure src/lib/atlasPlot.ts builds the strip: one dot per account with deterministic FNV-1a jitter, six axis segments aligned to the band edges plus a labeled 120+ overflow bin for the 1200 deci cap. The atlas mounts as a section above the console in App.tsx; dot clicks call the existing consoleStore.selectAccount, so E5 makes no store change and needs no E6 seam. **Rationale**: one vocabulary cannot drift; label and numbers from one twist object makes mislabeling structurally impossible; the band-aligned axis keeps the under 3 month mass legible across a 120 month range. **Trade-offs**: the researched 7-state nuances (drought ratio, negative_buffer to flood) retire in favor of the plain verdictBand answer; whole percents may not sum to 100; 4,500 SVG circles are memoized with a documented single-path fallback if a twist-drag frame exceeds 50 ms. ``` ## README wording contract (hand to the doc agent; they own README.md) The two README paragraphs (Storm Atlas section and the pipeline paragraph) should say, in the repo's voice: the atlas summarizes all 4,500 profiles into the **five verdict bands** (critical, storm warning, watch, fair skies, clear) and renders a **strip plot**: every account is one dot positioned by months of runway on an axis split at the verdict band edges with a labeled 120+ segment for the capped runway. The headline quotes the share of accounts under 3 months of runway, labeled honestly as at baseline or under a specific twist (the same twist the console ran). Clicking a dot selects that account in the console. Summary math stays in pure modules (`summarizeStormAtlas`, `accountsInBand`, `buildAtlasPlot`); the components read finished numbers. Also: drop the "seven cell grid" and "seven weather states" phrasing wherever it appears (lines ~43 and ~51-53), and flag the same stale vocabulary in `docs/devpost.md` line 89.

At judging a judge picks an `account_id` and a twist card, and the engine runs live in about five minutes: 1. **Know the customer.** Any account shows typical income I, fixed costs F, spending S, savings buffer B, household bills H, loan payment P, gap, and months of runway, all from the precomputed profile artifact. 2. **Take a shock.** A shock (job loss with EI at 55 percent, bills up 15 percent, a one-off repair, or a mix) changes income or spending and the runway recomputes with the judge's branch rules. 3. **Make a plan.** A goal plan (emergency fund) and a backup plan (if the shock lands) built from the same numbers. The one-minute pitch opens with the Storm Atlas: the runway distribution across all 4,500 accounts, then one click drills into any account for the live twist. Every number a judge sees traces back to source rows through provenance checksums. The orbit game and the findings-first report framing are dropped as surfaces; their machinery may be reused internally. ## Hard constraints - **Judge definitions are the contract.** I, F, S, B, H, P and the runway come from docs/tangerine-challenge.md. No float may decide a branch. - **Deterministic offline artifact.** profiles.json carries no timestamps, no randomness, and no floats; two consecutive builds are byte identical. All data is bundled for an offline booth. - **Checksummed sources fail loud.** The three canonical CSVs are verified against data/tangerine/SHA256SUMS before any row is read. - **Any account must work.** All 4500 accounts, including the five edge flags (pensioner, thin history, zero income, defaulted loan, negative buffer), must render without a special case. - **One weather vocabulary.** src/lib/verdict.ts owns the five bands (critical, storm warning, watch, fair skies, clear) over integer deci months (10, 30, 60, 120).
